core.title: Imports point inward through the layer hierarchy
core.given: A non-test source module, in any code tree the layer rules apply to (shared/commons and feature code alike), that the profile's role assignment places in a layer role
core.when: It imports another project module (an import that resolves inside the project graph, not an external package)
core.then: The import MUST point inward: presentation -> application -> domain; integration -> application, domain; only the composition root may reach any layer.
prefer: When an inner layer needs an outer capability, use an existing inward-facing port.
During GREEN: introduce the smallest missing port only when the current behavior cannot otherwise be implemented correctly, and limit its contract to what the acceptance requires.
During GREEN: reuse the nearest existing compliant dependency path (shared phase-loop policy).
avoid: Reclassifying or merging layers merely to make one import legal.
Adding an outward-pointing dependency as a temporary step.
Spreading 'knows everything' wiring outside the composition root.
Broadening the change by redesigning adjacent modules (shared phase-loop policy: do not broaden).
unless: Test files (unit, acceptance and e2e test roles) and the stack's excluded vendored/build trees are never scanned.
Imports of external packages, recognised by the stack's external-import idiom, resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
A file that the role assignment places in no layer role is outside these rules, not in violation.
core.why: It governs feature code too, where most layering damage happens. The composition-root exemption makes it workable: something must know about everything, and confining that to the composition root is the point of having one.
evidence: Every affected import still points in an allowed direction (no finding from the stack's layer-hierarchy import check).
verification: The check resolves each project import of an in-scope file to its target layer role and flags an edge the hierarchy does not permit.
Allowed edges (inward import): presentation -> application -> domain; integration -> application, domain. This is the permitted direction.
Composition-root exemption: the composition root may import any layer.
Scope: skip test files and the excluded vendored/build trees; skip external-package imports; files with no layer role are out of scope, not violations.

fires: A domain module imports an application, integration, presentation or composition-root module.
An application module imports from presentation or integration.
An integration module imports from presentation.
A feature module (not only shared/commons code) has an import whose target layer is outward of its own layer.
A change moves or edits code so that an existing import of an in-scope file is affected.
doesNotFire: The composition root imports any layer to wire them together.
A test file imports across layers.
Files under the stack's excluded vendored/build trees.
An import of an external package (outside the project graph).
A file that is assigned no layer role.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's layer roles and their local names, covering presentation, application, domain, integration and the composition root.
The stack's local name for the composition root that is exempt from the hierarchy.
How a file is assigned to a layer role, and that a file with no layer role is out of scope rather than a violation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Layer read from the file path's layer segment, in commons and feature code alike; files without a layer segment are out of scope.

profileRequirements.meaning: The code trees to which the layer rule applies.
How an import of an external package (outside the project graph, not layer-checked) is distinguished from a project import.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Bare npm package specifier import (outside the project graph); project imports are non-bare-npm imports.

profileRequirements.meaning: The vendored/build trees that are never scanned.

neutralityNotes: The Bun activation fact 'layer' is mapped to the closed fact 'role' (assembly -> composition_root). Test-file identification is expressed through the test roles; Bun gives no concrete suffix, so no suffix key is required. The Bun shared node policy.phase-loop ('During GREEN: reuse the nearest existing compliant dependency path. Do not broaden: do not redesign adjacent modules. Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.') is stack-neutral and is carried into the core explicitly with its original scoping: reuse-nearest-path (GREEN-scoped) as prefer[2], no-adjacent-redesign (no phase restriction) as avoid[3], and the proof as evidence[1]. It is not a numbered item of this rule, so it has no classification entry of its own. Nothing else had to stay Bun-specific beyond the detector/validator id.
